content: Autoimmune type 1 diabetes represents approximately 5-10% of all diagnosed diabetes cases. This condition arises due to the immune system's targeted destruction of pancreatic β-cells, which are responsible for producing insulin. The resulting damage leads to a deficiency in insulin production. Genetic predisposition plays a significant role in the development of type 1 diabetes, with specific human leukocyte antigen (HLA) haplotypes, such as HLA-DR and HLA-DQ, being strongly associated with increased susceptibility. High-risk alleles include DRB10301 and DQB10201, collectively referred to as DR3-DQ2, as well as DRB10401 and DQB10302, known as DR4-DQ8. Testing for the presence of autoantibodies is a valuable diagnostic tool for identifying individuals at risk, particularly in those who have a family history of autoimmune disorders.
